headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared text/file flows between ms-swift and pipecat; capability conflict is limited by non-overlapping write surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ms-swift reads/writes files and stdin/stdout, while pipecat uses a shared bus and multiple transports. If ms-swift output is fed into pipecat without sanitization, attacker-controlled text can be treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed, so uncertainty pushes severity up from low.
conditions: IF ms-swift output is routed into pipecat prompts or tool messages without filtering, injection is possible.
IF a shared bus carries raw model text between the agents, instruction hijacking becomes plausible.
mitigations: Insert a strict content filter between agents.
Wrap ms-swift outputs in a non-executable schema.
Disable raw prompt forwarding on the shared bus.
Log and review any instruction-like tokens before forwarding.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and secrets like hub_token/sdk-token; pipecat touches conversation state and analytics/metrics and can call third-party APIs. A shared workspace or bus could leak sensitive content from ms-swift into pipecat outputs or upstream services. No direct isolation is documented, so the safer medium rating applies.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or bus, ms-swift artifacts can be exposed to pipecat.
IF pipecat forwards conversation state to external APIs, any imported sensitive text can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials immediately.
Remove secrets from any shared directory.
Turn off analytics for sensitive runs.
Use redaction before passing text to pipecat.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift has filesystem write and shell execution, but pipecat's documented surfaces emphasize transports and API calls rather than local file writes. Because overlapping mutable write targets are not documented, a direct conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains, but the pair does not show the high-risk same-directory write pattern.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto one mutable git or cache path, conflicts increase.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Run each agent under separate OS users.
Avoid shared caches for generated artifacts.
Add file-locking around any common path.
requires-engineering: introduce a coordinator with explicit locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ms-swift can emit model outputs and pipecat can route them through voice/chat pipelines and external services. If pipecat treats ms-swift text as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or user-facing responses. The pathway is plausible in default integration patterns, but not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF pipecat consumes ms-swift text without a verification step, hallucinations can propagate.
IF downstream services act on that text, the cascade can affect user-visible outputs or actions.
mitigations: Add a verification step before forwarding outputs.
Require citations or structured fields from ms-swift.
Gate downstream actions behind human approval.
Reject low-confidence or unstructured responses.
requires-engineering: implement end-to-end provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: ms-swift explicitly handles hub_token and sdk-token plus datasets/checkpoints/logs, while pipecat handles conversation state and analytics/metrics. The profiles do not state residency or certification mismatches, so only a documented-gap risk exists. Because the compliance pathway is not directly specified, low is appropriate rather than medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ms-swift artifacts and then routed through pipecat APIs, policy review is required.
IF retention settings differ between the two systems, deletion/export obligations can diverge.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it.
Avoid sending regulated data through pipecat APIs.
Set matching retention windows.
Document deletion/export handling for both systems.
requires-engineering: obtain vendor compliance attestations.
